reviews.author: filmtravel101

reviews.title: Indicative of a major identity problem for future projects
reviews.review:
After seeing Supergirl last night in the theater I have to say two things - 1) it was a fun summer flick; 2) DCU needs to find it's footing fast.

Regarding the first thing - Supergirl is a fun movie. It's not too long, it's not dull, it's funny, it's colorful, it's dynamic, the action is decent, the direction is not bad... all in all it's a movie literally made for a hot summer night in the theater where you switch you brain off for an hour and a half. If this was a standalone adventure that would have been enough.

However, the movie tackles incredibly difficult subjects without any real weight to the subject matter. There a few moments that really shine and those are the moments that make you wonder what kind of movie this would have been if the movie gave all of it's subject matter the same treatment. Certain themes were introduced too late and were not given enough time to develop properly, other themes were present from the start but were not explored enough at all.

There are moments where the movie tries to be narratively dark and difficult but it never really leans into the psychology of these scene or the characters that should feel said difficulty, leaving the viewer indifferent to what was going on.

As a result Supergirl lacks emotional and dramatic depth. For the themes it tries to deal with it is incredibly one-dimensional.

On the acting side there is little to be said. Alcock carries the movie on her shoulders with little help from others. Momoa is there playing himself as usual, while the villains are never truly explored nor are they given any real sense of agency. It feels as if they were there because the movie needed a villain. Everything that would have made those villains remotely interesting is never explored enough and is at times derivative of movies that tackled similar issues with much more success.

The dynamic between the two main protagonists is intriguing but never really goes anywhere. The ending carries no dramatic weight and leaves the viewer with simple acceptance of what is shown. It's a form of take it or leave it resolution.

Music is bland and not innovative, no catchy tunes, nothing memorable, simply serviceable. The editing could have been better as there are certain segments where scenes were very fast, almost to the point of inability to fully follow what was happening.

All this brings us to my second point. Superman was not far from any of these complaints. Supergirl emphasises the problems that arose in Superman. These movies function well together as they share much of the same DNA, but they are the kind of movies that have nothing important to say. They deal with incredibly complex and layered characters; characters that have to fight with important sociological and existential issues. DCU has withered them down to fun summer flicks that say nothing and mean nothing.

It if imperative that the future movies of the DCU give their characters more to do that just fly around and have cool colorful scenes and quippy one-liners.

The S on their chest is not an S, it's a symbol of hope. I thing it's high time that DCU get's that right.

If not, they could be looking at a flop that will, once again, be rebooted and we will be left with a cool fun action move to watch on a lazy Sunday afternoon. If I wanted that I would have watched the Justice league cartoons. They at least understand their characters.

reviews.title: Superman's Cousin Flies Back on the Big Screen
reviews.review:
Marking the second installment in the DC Universe, Supergirl has come out for the whole world to see. Focused on Superman's cousin Kara Zor-El this time around, the film depicts said title character embarking on a quest of vengeance with an unlikely companion. Keeping the general light hearted yet brutally mature tone of James Gunn's Superman film, Supergirl manages to weave its story through Kara having to grow up and take some responsibility for herself. In being one of Krypton's last survivors, the filmmakers appropriately established her as being far more jaded and cynical than Clark Kent. It's only until she goes on her journey of vengeance against the ruthless Krem that she has to self reflect on what form of justice she believes in, especially as the similarly determined Ruthye Marye Knoll tags along with her.

The conflicting bond between Kara and Ruthye is what largely carries the feature throughout the journey, and their chemistry grows stronger as they learn from one another about how to become better people regardless of their goals, especially in regards to avenging loved ones. Admittedly, aside from Krem and Clark Kent himself, those two are the most relevant characters in the film's present day. While part of Kara's goal to get back at Krem comes from him attacking her pet dog Krypto, other characters like Lobo, Bomar and Mareck are largely utilized for plot relevance once the stakes get high. That said, a large part of what made Kara into who she was comes through in unnerving flashbacks featuring her parents Zor-El and Alura In-Ze, further emphasizing how tragic Kara's path became as her home world fell apart.

Other notable qualities that help the film out range from the banger soundtrack, solid computer animation and general scale & scope of each distinctive planet. The art direction in particular stands out in differentiating specific color palettes in suns that affect Kryptonians, specifically in how Kara spends her time getting drunk on red sun planets and how she would become severely weakened on green sun planets. It's little details like that which go a long way in emphasizing Kara's strengths, weaknesses and hurdles between various worlds that she has no choice but to grow accustomed to. All this and more to prove that Supergirl is a solid enough take on the iconic super heroine whilst fitting into a newly welcomed cinematic universe for the DC gang. Here's hoping more fun filled adventures with Kara can come swooping in on the big screen soon.

reviews.review: I enjoyed this more than I expected. I liked the Krypton flashbacks, the different coloured suns and how they affected her, and the way each planet had its own look and atmosphere. There is a good variety of aliens, Lobo looks cool, and the fight scenes are made even better by the music choices. It kept me interested throughout and did not feel too long. My main issue was the villain, who was boring, annoying, and built around the same tired "joking while being evil" cliché. reviews.title: A much needed Supergirl movie
reviews.review:
Expecting every superhero movie to have an incredibly deep character arc, a larger-than-life supervillain, and world-ending stakes is unrealistic. Not every film needs to follow the same formula.

Supergirl tells a genuinely good story, looks visually stunning, and I really appreciated how it explored a real-world issue through an intergalactic setting. It added a layer of relatability without taking away from the fun and adventure.

Milly Alcock was exceptional as Supergirl. She portrayed Kara with absolute grace, perfectly balancing vulnerability, confidence, and emotional depth, making the character feel authentic and compelling.

Sure, there are things that could have been better, but if you're simply looking for a fun, heartfelt superhero movie with great visuals, a meaningful story, and a fantastic lead performance, this is a 10/10 for me.

reviews.title: Don't freak out
reviews.review:
Greetings again from the darkness. Craig Gillespie previously directed I, TONYA (2017) and LARS AND THE REAL GIRL (2007), among other projects, and it's perhaps those two films - both featuring odd outsiders - that motivated producer James Gunn to choose him to helm the feature film that brings DC's Supergirl back to the big screen. The screenplay is by Ana Nogueira, and of course features characters originated by Jerry Siegel and Joel Shuster, with the key source material being the comic, "Supergirl: Woman of Tomorrow".

Seeing as I'm neither a comic book fanatic nor a fan of the 1984 SUPERGIRL film starring Helen Slater (with the exception of Brenda Vaccaro's performance), it's safe to say I carried no heightened expectations into the theater. On the bright side, it's quite entertaining to see Milly Alcock ("Sirens", "House of the Dragon") play Kara Zor-El as a not-so-Super girl trying to numb the pain of the tragedy that took her parents and home planet, Krypton. We see her younger days via periodic flashbacks with David Krumholtz and Emily Beecham as her parents. We also learn why they shipped her and her pet dog Krypto off to Earth to meet her cousin, Superman (David Corenswet) aka Clark Kent. He, of course, was raised in Kansas, creating the contrast between the two characters.

The one bit of advice mom gave Kara was to "be nice" and help others. That's not so easy to do whilst on an intergalactic mind-numbing bender, but Kara continually rises to the occasion. The different effects of red sun and yellow sun become quite obvious, and it's crossing paths with Ruthye (Eve Ridley) that drives the key story lines. An actor I've always admired, Matthias Schoenaerts, plays the face-studded vile villain Krem - the vicious dude who slaughtered Ruthye's family, setting her off on a revenge mission, armed only with a prized sword handcrafted by her slain father. As savage as Krem is, we all recognize that a standout villain is vital to a standout superhero movie, and Krem simply falls short. On this interplanetary road trip, Kara and Ruthye encounter a slew of aliens who all look like castoffs from the Star Wars casino ... but also with Lobo, an immortal intergalactic bounty hunter and stogie smoking hog rider. Lobo is played by Jason Mamoa, and the character seems forcibly wedged into the story for the sole purpose of having Mr. Mamoa on a poster. He makes an excellent bad boy, even if he doesn't really fit here.

Krypto the superdog plays near-dead for most of the film, but does have some excitable moments ... creating an excellent 'pink eye' joke. Some may compare this to CAPTAIN MARVEL (2019) or the most recent SUPERMAN (2025), but the messy CGI fight scenes and weak story prevent this one from reaching those levels. Milly Alcock's take on Supergirl gets too few chances to play against Corenswet's Superman, and the film suffers because of it. Composer Claudia Sarne (THE BOOK OF ELI, 2010) delivers a fitting electronic score, but the needle drops seem to be trying too hard. It's likely huge comic book fans will have a different take on the film, and that's as it should be.

In theaters beginning June 26, 2026.

reviews.title: Keeps the franchise aloft
reviews.review:
Supergirl, who was briefly seen at the end of last year's Superman, here takes center stage in a story of her life and (mis)adventures. Kara-El is initially an interplantery party girl/binge drinker whose spacecraft home resembles an RV used for a wild spring break outing.

Before long, circumstances give her an occasion to rise to. Traveling to a variety of worlds, she has a variety of encounters that bring to mind a variety of sci-fi universes, such as "Star Wars", "Guardians of the Galaxy", and "Blade Runner".

While the narrative slows at times, there are scenes that feel either murky or over-stylized, and there's a few plot holes, Milly Alcock solidly grounds the film with her multifaceted portrayal of a powerful (and flawed) person meandering through life and wrestling with past loses. Several supporting characters are good as well. Some overdone and needlessly unpleasant stuff isn't too big a distraction from the entertaining main story. Ands there's some serious girl power!

Good for superhero and sci-fi fans alike.

reviews.title: Ignore Review Bombers, Form Your Own Opinion
reviews.review: Supergirl is the second film entry into the DCU following the 2025 summer blockbuster film Superman. It's directed by Craig Gillespie, stars Milly Alcock as Supergirl and Eve Ridley as Ruthye. It was originally titled "Supergirl: Woman of Tomorrow" taking the title of its main inspiration, Supergirl: The Woman of Tomorrow, the award winning comic written by Tom King and illustrated by Bilquis Evely. From the moment I read the original title of the film it instantly became one of my most anticipated films of 2026 as Woman of Tomorrow is one of my favorite comic runs ever. After Superman directed by James Gunn, Gunn's involvement in this film and the original title, I assumed he'd fully embrace what made Woman of Tomorrow so special and translate it to screen. Anyone who has read the comic knows that the first thing that comes to mind when it's mentioned is the colorful and stunning artwork by Bilquis Evely. So from the beginning my expectations for this films visuals were set sky high. Story wise, the comic is a cosmic roadtrip story that has heavy western influences. It takes place on various planets all unique in their own way and rich with their own cultures. The recipe for a film is essentially written already thanks to Tom King. If the director used the comic as a storyboard and made an attempt at adapting the visuals we'd be looking at a phenomenal film. And it's ironic because simultaneously my favorite and least favorite aspect of this film is how it adapted the Woman of Tomorrow comic to screen. There's stretches here and there that are extremely faithful to the comic and had the fan in me smiling. Specifically the first act of the film is relatively faithful and had my expectations high for the rest. But eventually it settled in to your typical comic book film and made unnecessary changes to the source material only to the detriment of the film. For example and probably the most damning is instead of having the planet with the green sun a colorful, vast and lush jungle full of apex predators. It's instead a barren wasteland with nothing but dust around creating a completely uninteresting world. Not only is it visually unappealing but doing so you lose the impactful scene of Rutheye protecting Kara from the predators as they wait for the sun to set. Just a small change like that really undermines Rutheyes character and makes her feel like less of a help and more of a burden. By far the biggest disappointment though is the overall aesthetic and color grading of the film. While near impossible to translate Bilquis Evely's art to film, there was hardly even an attempt. So many of the scenes are extremely dark and suffer from a lack of proper lighting. Then when there is a bright light source it tends to be overexposed completely blocking the view of characters faces. By far the biggest example of the lighting problems and visual issues is the final fight sequence. It's on the same barren planet and it ends up making for an extremely anti climactic end fight visually and emotionally. The lighting and setting isn't the largest issue with said scene though. There's a needle drop in this scene that may genuinely go down as one of the worst ever. It's a needle drop of The Middle by "Jimmy Eat World" covered by "Kelty Greye"and "KidMotel". The scene is from Rutheye's perspective and clearly the director was attempting to use soundtrack dissonance to juxtapose the situation she was in. But all it achieves is completely taking the viewer out of the moment and turns what could've been a decent scene into a laughably bad one. Another major issue this film has is with its villain. Krem, similarly to the comics is just a really bland and uninspired villain. He has no real motivation and no backstory, he's just evil for the sake of the plot. I can't necessarily blame anyone for that as he's exactly like that in the comic. Although, his design is pretty atrocious in the film as it feels extremely over designed just for the sake of him standing out. Now, with all my complaints out of the way I have to give credit where it's due. Milly Alcock is a completely serviceable Supergirl and I can't wait to see her in future projects. Eve Ridley as Rutheye was great and aside from writing problems was as accurate as can be. And lastly, Jason Mamoa as Lobo is just absolutely incredible. He really was born to play the role as he feels like someone shook a comic book and he came falling out. While I'm extremely critical of this film, it's only because I see the potential this film had. With that being said, while not being great it's nowhere near as bad as some people seem to think it is. It's a perfectly acceptable comic book film that doesn't try to reinvent the wheel for better and worse at times.

reviews.title: Supergirl (2026)
reviews.review:
Rating: 0/10

This didn't feel like a Supergirl movie. It felt like Guardians of the Galaxy with Supergirl dropped into it.

The movie skips over much of Kara's origin and rushes straight into the main story, leaving very little time to establish her character or make the audience emotionally invested.

Spoilers ahead:

The story moves from one cosmic adventure to the next without giving many of the emotional moments room to breathe. The final battle is packed with large-scale visual effects, but it didn't have much emotional impact for me because I never felt connected to the journey. Several major plot reveals happen so quickly that they don't land as strongly as they could have.

The tone leans heavily into space adventure and humor, making it feel closer to Guardians of the Galaxy than a traditional Supergirl story. Instead of creating its own identity, it often feels like it's borrowing that style.

Overall, it felt like style over substance. If you wanted a more character-focused or comic-inspired Supergirl film, this version may be disappointing.

The overall story is fine, I think it could have had a bit more depth to it. Backstory actually really enjoyable and just the right amount of time on it. Ruthye is a pain, sorry an unbearable character that seems to serve as a moral narrative on vengeance yet totally disregarded later. She's boring and annoying.

The main villain Krem, crap to be honest, forgettable and the motive was so meh, when I say that HIS motive was solely on the motive of kidnapping the girls and is just a "bad guy". Definitely should have leaned into the slavery bit that could have been great. Finally the script is quite poor, kinda cringe dialogue at times.

It's unfortunate because I feel it could have been much stronger, but i am excited to see more Supergirl with a different script, 6/10.

There were a few things I didn't like, such as the changes they made to Krypton and its history, but I can accept that as a different interpretation.

I also thought the villain was better than people give him credit for. He was ruthless, had a good sense of humor, and made for an entertaining antagonist. Overall, I had a good time with the movie, and I think it deserves a lot more credit than it's getting.

reviews.title: One of the worst superhero movies of all time
reviews.review:
This movie is about a cynical girl with super powers who do not care about anything but party and drinking. Then her dog get hurt and she needs to avenge the doggy. That is the movie. It is all filmed through muddy water, and the script is so bad I cannot believe it was green-lit. The acting abysmal. The directing horrid.

reviews.author: CosmosNamob

reviews.title: Milly Alcock is excellent, and it's a blast watching Supergirl cut loose
reviews.review:
First off, this movie deserves BIG credit for taking the character of Supergirl seriously, not just some fluffy sidebar to Superman. Milly Alcock is great as the lead and this is a storyline and production at the same level of commitment as last year's Superman. And just so that I don't forget to say this, the final extended battle scene where she suits up and cuts loose on the army of villains is terrific. It's worth the price of admission. One essential feature of that climatic scene is how it leans all the way in to her superspeed: she turns into a whirling hurricane of vengeance who seems to be everywhere at once. Yes, superhero movies are basically popcorn fare, but THIS is why we go to them.

In the first 'Supergirl' way back in 1984, Helen Slater looked the part for sure but was stuck with a terrible script and low-budget effects. In 'The Flash' (2013), Sasha Calle as an alternate-universe Supergirl was the best thing about that mess of a movie, but was brutally tossed aside as if she didn't really matter. This new one is different: it isn't your stereotypical cheerful, sunny Supergirl, but that gives the story more material to work through. Unlike cousin Clark, who wants to fix everything peacefully, she has no trouble wading into ultra-violent action. But it's great to see Milly Alcock bring this very different Kara Zor-el to life. The underlying theme of this movie (which is a decent one) is to see her work through and come to terms with her history of grief, anger, sadness, and confusion. She lost her home and her family to natural disaster and doesn't necessarily like what she had to trade it in for.

If you check out the bar chart of viewer ratings, my advice is to cut out all the votes in both the '1' and '10' bins (the trolls and antitrolls) and look at the rest. The answer is 7/10 and I think that's about where it belongs. The characters are fun if typical but the plot is a bit of a mess -- too many cycles of 'now she's up, now she's down', what/where is happening -- it just needs a cleaner, clearer storyline. As the smarmy villain Krem, Matthias Schoenaerts clearly has fun overacting but the character never gets beyond conventional. As Lobo, Jason Momoa seems to be there just to bring in the fanboys. He doesn't actually play much of a role in what happens. I'd rather have seen that time devoted to Kara's character development. As Ruthye, Eve Ridley is fine, but again her character doesn't have more than (dare I say it) comic-book depth.

Two minor points I noticed: one is a new and better explanation for why Kara is younger than Clark: she was actually born on Argo City 8 years AFTER the destruction of Krypton. That makes a lot more sense than the travel-delay, Negative Zone stuff that we were given before. The second thing is just a single line of dialog by Kara's mother watching baby Kal-el's capsule being launched to Earth, which confirms what we were shown in last year's Superman: Jor-el intended him to conquer Earth as an overlord. That is, his parents weren't nice at all.

I hope we get to see this Kara again. It probably won't be as THE main character, but tram-ups will do if that's what we get.

reviews.author: runethestrong

reviews.title: Supergirl Was Never Meant for a Basic Audience
reviews.review:
There will likely be a lot of misogynistic opinions about this movie, and some people might go in already deciding they won't like it because it's not "basic" enough for them. But if you go in with an open mind, Supergirl really is worth it.

This movie carries a lot of emotion built from hardship, struggle, and quiet strength. The humour, the story, and the character growth all come from that foundation. It's not just about power-it's about what it takes to keep going when life keeps breaking you down.

Superman represents a hero who teaches kindness. Supergirl represents something different but just as important: how to stay strong, how to protect others, and how to guard your heart while still choosing to be good in a harsh world. She shows how to carry pain without letting it turn you cold.

One moment that stuck with me was hearing two teenage boys say Supergirl should've just been a side character to Superman as they walked out of the cinema. It honestly says a lot about how female-led superhero stories are still not always given a fair chance, no matter how much depth they offer.

Because this story does have depth-more than people expect if they walk in with bias. If you actually want a film with meaning, emotional weight, and a message that stays with you after the credits, then give Supergirl a real chance.

reviews.title: Not that bad
reviews.review: With all the bad review online, you would think this movie was as bad as the Catwoman movie. I do wish everyone would stop comparing it to Gog. Just because it's in space and has a modern soundtrack doesn't make it the same. I do feel like a lot of people missed the point of the movie. Or they just never had to deal with real grief and feeling out of place at the same time. I think people wanted a hardcore villain. When the main focus was overcoming your emotions to become the person you are meant to be. It's a good starting point for this character. When your cousin is Supman. It show different side of how to be a good person. Without having to be super polite and caring about how people see you.
reviews.author: Anobodywholikesmovies

reviews.title: Another DC disappointment
reviews.review:
Like many other reviewers I went to see this with big expectations. That may color my review; but, this is easily the worst DC movie I can remember seeing. It suffers from a trifecta of failure. The most disappointing aspect of this film is the screenplay. The story is thin, devoid of any real energy or direction and simply meanders from subplot to the next hoping the actors will bring some life to the film. Whatever DC Studios paid the writers (Ana Nogueira, Jerry Siegel & Joe Shuster) it was way too much. The film, as a whole, seems to suffer a lack of vision and connection between parts; for this I blame the director, Craig Gillespie. It is still a mystery why he was given responsibility for this film. His past work doesn't really screen engaging drama or gripping action. The last major failure of the film is the acting. While several have some serious dramatic acting in their histories many of the leads simply fail to grab the audience. While Milly Alcock is not the worst of the bunch, given her time on screen her weak performance (which is probably best described as a "moody teen in a cellphone commercial") drags the film down. Her emotions fail to seem sincere and her attempt at snappy dialogue seems more like smirky adolescent whining than deep emotional response.

This film is not worth watching. It is sad that DC Studios does not take their IP more seriously. I left the theater wondering if anyone involved actually read the comics or any DC hero comic for that matter.

reviews.title: Not bad
reviews.review: Overall, a reasonably enjoyable movie. Decent motivating factors, good action. But it all felt contrived, with a lot of coincidences and way too much effort to justify her being a disturbed girl who just wants to get drunk and avoid being a hero. Interesting that the villain leads a group of men who capture women, and there isn't really a decent man in the whole movie except for a minute of talking with Superman. At least they didn't make her a lesbian.

reviews.author: keithhaugen

reviews.title: Apparently This Was a Supergirl Movie. Allegedly
reviews.review:
This isn't a **Supergirl** movie.

It's a movie where someone found a blonde woman, gave her a cape, and hoped nobody in the audience had ever opened a DC comic.

James Gunn didn't just set this movie up to fail-he practically handed it a shovel, watched it dig its own grave, and then rolled the credits.

Now, class, let's all repeat together:

* Kryptonians are basically gods under a yellow sun.

* A green star (assuming those even work the way this movie thinks they do) doesn't magically turn them into wet tissue paper.

* Kryptonians move at relativistic speeds. They don't queue up politely to exchange punches with random space hooligans.

* A Kryptonian doesn't need an extended action sequence to defeat discount space pirates. Five seconds. Done.

* Their heat vision is literally hotter than stars, yet somehow everyone survives long enough for another awkward fight scene.

* Lobo is immortal. You don't stop him with a fancy metal cage like you've trapped an overgrown raccoon.

Excellent. Gold stars for everyone except the screenplay.

Let's try another lesson:

* Heroes are called heroes for a reason.

* They put others before themselves.

* They inspire hope.

* They don't casually cross moral lines because the plot couldn't think of anything more interesting.

Congratulations! You've now demonstrated a better understanding of superhero storytelling than this script.

One final exercise:

* Space pirates carrying laser rifles generally aren't terrified of... steel swords.

Who knew?

The plot wanders around the galaxy looking for a destination and never finds one. Characters appear to exist because the payroll department insisted on paying somebody. There's no meaningful character growth, no satisfying redemption arc, no emotional payoff-just scene after scene of "stuff happening."

The most impressive superpower on display is the script's ability to ignore decades of established Kryptonian lore whenever it's inconvenient.

By the end, the 1984 *Supergirl* movie starts looking less like a guilty pleasure and more like a misunderstood cinematic masterpiece deserving of a retrospective at the Oscars.

The whole production feels like nobody involved stopped to ask a dangerous question:

*"Has anyone here actually read a Supergirl comic?"*

Apparently not.

The lead isn't written as Supergirl so much as someone cosplaying a completely different character who occasionally remembers to wear the "S" symbol. Also the main lead Milly Alcock is rather unpleasant & uneasy on the eyes, if you know what I mean.

As for James Gunn... if this is the blueprint for the new DC Universe, then somewhere the Phantom Zone is filing a copyright claim for crimes against Krypton.

At this point, "Restore the Snyderverse" has gone from internet meme to emergency contingency plan.

**Rating:** 1/10.

No point for the cape.

One point because Krypto is innocent in all of this.

reviews.title: Fun & Overhated!
reviews.review:
It's unfortunate how poorly the response has been to this movie. It's not groundbreaking by any means, but I can't say I was bored at any moment.

The biggest gripes I can see is the plot was simplistic and the villain wasn't layered. However, that type of villain isn't needed for every story. Plus, you can tell the actor portraying had a great time performing and I had good time with him. But the pacing was fine, performances were solid, action was fun and the comedy well timed. Plus we got to spend some time on Krypton!

All in all, it's not great but not at all a bad movie. 7/10 feels the perfect rating and I'm really excited to see where Milly goes with Supergirl, because she was absolutely perfect!

reviews.author: malichi-71751

reviews.title: Very poorly lit
reviews.review:
With social media inundated with bad faith people attacking Milly Alcock, my interest in Supergirl increased, it only made me want to see the movie more. It is like when your parents say stay away from this guy, don't you ever do this, and you run to that person and those things. Anyway I had seen her in the recent Superman movie and was very impressed, just as I was impressed with her in House of the Dragon.

From the very moment you see her in Supergirl it is obvious Milly Alock is a movie star through and through. She is effortlessly charismatic, fun to watch, and very photogenic. I would even go so far as to say she has Han Solo or Indiana Jones style energy. Obviously she is a beautiful blond woman but she truly is a female version of Harrison Ford. She has that exact same kind of energy.

I enjoyed seeing all the space aliens and spaceships and scenes on other planets. I did not mind at all that very little of the movie takes place on Earth. Eve Ridley is excellent as Ruthye the sword bearing young avenger. I don't know what the hell Jason Momoa was supposed to be. I guess fans of comic books know who Lobo is and may love him but he means nothing to me.

Folks have become accustomed to superhero films and sci fi films where the hero must rescue the universe from total destruction, so it was refreshing to see a movie where it was mostly about saving a dog and a young woman's desire for revenge.

The only real problem I have with the movie is they freaking left the lights off. There are all these seemingly bone crushing scenes of people kicking ass but I mostly could not see what the heck was going on. The film is very poorly lit and this ruined all the scenes where people were fighting.

Another thing I can't help mentioning. Back before the movie came out and all you could see were trailers for it, I said what the heck, it looks like for most of the movie she doesn't even wear the Supergirl outfit and people jumped on me. It turns out that this is the case. Now I don't mind. She's super enough no matter what she wears.

Sadly we get to see the very underwhelming David Corenswet again. It was a mistake to put him in this movie. He is so totally upstaged by Alcock. Superman is supposed to be the greatest of all superheroes and here as in Superman 2025 he looks like a busboy or a friend who came over to help you move. He is not the Superman Reeve and Cavill were. You saw them you instantly felt they were Superman. This guy completely lacks the charisma and self confidence required for the role, and seeing him in scenes with Alcock only drives the point home further.

In summary, a fine film, undone only by how terribly lit it is. Hopefully at some point the director will explain why he filmed it this way.
reviews.author: hswasserman

reviews.title: A swing and a miss we saw coming a mile away
reviews.review:
A messy, identity-less remix of Guardians of the Galaxy and Mad Max that completely strips away the core optimism of the character. Making Kara a sullen, cynical brat kills the emotional weight of the comic book it's supposedly adapting. The script is entirely derivative, the action is muddled, and Matthias Schoenaerts is completely wasted on an underwhelming, poorly defined villain. Milly Alcock's performance is gratingly one-note, cementing a narrative that feels entirely redundant.

Skip this one, the number of obvious shills out there is crazy.
reviews.author: SquirrelJam

reviews.title: Ignore the pile-on, this is a genuinely fun space adventure
reviews.review:
I went in expecting the disaster the internet promised and walked out having a great time. Milly Alcock is the whole thing, she plays Kara as jaded, funny, and a little wrecked, and she carries scenes that a lesser lead would have dropped. The cosmic road-trip structure gives the movie room to breathe, Momoa's Lobo is a blast every second he's on screen, and Krypto earns every reaction he gets.

Yes, some of the space environments look flat, and the flashbacks land at an odd point in the runtime. Fair criticisms. But I don't understand how those add up to the "disaster" framing this movie has been getting. I've sat through plenty of Marvel films with the exact same issues that nobody called career-enders. This one gave me nearly two hours of adventure, jokes that actually land, and a lead I want to follow into the next film.

Not a masterpiece and it isn't trying to be. It's a good time at the movies with an emotional core about grief that sneaks up on you. 8/10, and I'd watch it again.

reviews.title: Beyond krypton
reviews.review: Supergirl is stunning. The cosmic landscapes, alien worlds, and imaginative creatures create an expansive universe that feels fresh and exciting. The visual effects are impressive throughout, especially during the large-scale action sequences. Space battles, alien environments, and Supergirl's flight scenes are beautifully crafted, delivering the sense of wonder that fans expect from a major DC production.
reviews.author: AntoraD

reviews.title: DC accidentally made me care, but it's a franchise movie
reviews.review:
The biggest compliment I can give this movie is that I left wanting another Supergirl movie instead of another Superman movie. Milly Alcock absolutely carries this thing. Her Kara is messy, funny, emotionally constipated, permanently sleepdeprived and looks like she has been surviving exclusively on alien larvae gas station coffee and poor decisions. Finally, a multifacted person, instead of trying to make superman compelling(yeah it worked in the latest reboot, blame his chiseled jawline, Lois Lane with a brain and goofy underpants).

The kid is also surprisingly great. Hollywood's usual dumb boy on a quest routine has been replaced by a compelling kid who actually possesses a functioning frontal lobe and a backbone no less. The worldbuilding is pretty decent too. Different species, complex languages and cultures make the galaxy feel inhabited instead of funny stage dressing. Not devoid of tropes, but a better attempt than many others, and the soundtrack carries more on it's shoulders than it's probably credited for.

Then the screenplay remembers several executive meetings happened, and it needs to be marketable to children/puritan audiences/MEN. The movie repeatedly points out that Kara lives in Superman's shadow and is treated differently because she's a woman. Fair enough. Then it does exactly nothing with this and ends with her wearing the brand-approved miniskirt and heels while Superman gets practical boots. Apparently self-discovery has a licensing agreement. In this day and age, worthy of extensive ridicule.

Lobo shows up because the script briefly ran out of ideas. He's entertaining enough, and Momoa seems an obvious cast for a biker mercenary with a cigar. However his arrival feels less like a satisfying payoff and more like someone opening the emergency hatch, because they couldn't write a plot that a godlike Kryptonian could reasonably survive. You could've replaced Lason Loboa with Shadow the hedgehog and it would've done the job, I guess.

The morality is where things really become fascinating. Kara spends most of the movie beating everyone into AT LEAST a coma, then suddenly borrows Batman's stubborn morale for five minutes, tells the kid killing is bad, prevents her from doing it... and later kills the villain herself anyway. If that is supposed to lead up to some sort of superman VS his cooler cousin movie, I'm just giving up honestly. Give Kara her own moral compass and stop borrowing Bruce Wayne's diary. The movie even points out how stupid the argument is, doesn't actually have any moment that explains why she's dying on that hill, but keeps hammering it anyway.

The Mad Max aesthetic also starts drifting into "we have Mad Max at home." Not terrible, good villain cast. I'm just wondering if reminding people to go watch a more compelling movie was the intent behind it. Also, marketing Krypto that hard only for him to disappear for most of the runtime should probably qualify as false advertising.

Still, there's a genuinely great SuperWoman buried in here. Hopefully the sequel lets Kara figure out who she wants to be instead of asking the branding department first. This movie keeps being so close to sincerity and actually landing a point, but then franchise branding barges in and ruins the moment. Maybe DC hasn't made anything memorable or iconic in more than a decade, because they keep shoving their writers into a trolley problem where they're not allowed to disappoint anyone, so they end up vaguely annoying everyone.
